title: Manual dissection of the Schistosoma mansoni esophagus and back end for proteomic analysis
author: Leandro Xavier Neves
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tq2emye

steps.title: Prepare Petri dish for microscopy
steps.instruction: Prepare the Petri dish containing worms for observation under the stereomicroscope.

substeps.instruction: Remove the Petri dish from the ice bath.
Touch the dish against paper to remove excess water.
Place the dish under the stereomicroscope (e.g., Leica EZ4) and adjust the focus.

steps.title: Position male worm head
steps.instruction: Locate and stabilize a male parasite with an uncurled head/esophagus.

substeps.instruction: Increase lens magnification.
Use tweezers (e.g., Ideal Tak 7SG.CX.0) and scissors (e.g., John Weiss Vannas scissors) to keep the head in the field-of-view.

steps.title: Perform first incision
steps.instruction: Release the oral sucker by making an incision at its posterior.

substeps.instruction: Hold the parasite with tweezers at an angle (lateral view or suckers facing up) to clearly see the suckers.
Make the first incision (#1) at the posterior of the oral sucker.

steps.title: Excise the esophagus
steps.instruction: Cut off the esophagus (ESO) along the transverse gut.

substeps.instruction: Perform the second incision (#2) along the transverse gut where the dark pigmentation of hemozoin starts.
Ensure the ventral sucker is not cut off during this process.

steps.title: Collect ESO fragment
steps.instruction: Aspirate the detached ESO fragment and store it on ice.

substeps.instruction: Use a P20 micropipette to aspirate the ESO fragment with RNAlater solution.
Dispense the fragment into the ESO microtube.
Keep the tube on ice.
Ensure no other fragments or particulate material are aspirated.

steps.title: Excise and collect back end
steps.instruction: Remove the posterior third of the parasite body.

substeps.instruction: Perform the final cut (#3) to remove the posterior third of the parasite body.
Collect the back end (BE) fragment using tweezers.
Transfer the BE fragment to the BE microtube and keep it in the ice box.

steps.title: Repeat dissection for additional parasites
steps.instruction: Repeat the dissection process for other male parasites as needed.

substeps.instruction: If salt crystals form, immerse tweezers and scissors in a beaker of deionized water.
Dry tools with soft, lint-free paper before continuing.

steps.title: Manage temperature and materials
steps.instruction: Maintain sample temperature and cleanliness every 10 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Start a 10-minute countdown when the Petri dish is removed from ice.
Return the Petri dish to the ice once the 10-minute timer expires.
Transfer dissected worms to the 'dissected body' microtube and add new worms to the Petri dish for the next round.
If salt crystals accumulate in the RNAlater solution: discard the solution, wash the Petri dish with deionized water, dry with lint-free paper, and add fresh RNAlater solution.
